title: Voice-over of the LinkedIn film on MiroFish

en: What if you could ask thirty thinkers the same question, and watch them argue?
MiroFish is an open-source swarm intelligence engine. It builds a small society of AI agents, each with a persona and a memory.
Then it lets them loose on a simulated social network, built on OASIS from CAMEL-AI. They post, reply, like and dislike. You read what emerges.
I used it for Ecosophia, a map of one hundred and fifty-nine thinkers of political ecology.
Each agent gets one author's record: key ideas, books, and quarrels. Claude chooses the panel and the number of rounds, within a budget.
After the debate, every agent states a position from zero to one hundred. Schools take sides, and unexpected alliances appear.
On new nuclear, market liberals land at seventy-four, ecofeminists at ten. On factory farming, twenty-three agents out of twenty-four agree, then split over meat itself.
Each debate costs about two dollars, and every word is labelled as simulated.
Now imagine it elsewhere. Test a new flexibility product on simulated industrial sites, grid operators and aggregators.
Rehearse a public consultation before a battery project. Pre-test a message. Prepare a negotiation with every stakeholder in the room.
It is a mirror, not an oracle. But a fast, cheap mirror is already a lot.
So, what would you put in the room?
